explanation.headline: Sevoflurane is not on FDA's shortage list; Corvale East has 4.6 days on hand of the 1 mL/mL 250 mL presentation and Corvale General has 18.4 days, so a transfer of 37 units is the top option

sentences.text: FDA's records show sevoflurane is not on the drug shortage list as of 2026-10-21.
Corvale East holds 41 units of sevoflurane 1 mL/mL 250 mL with daily use of 9, giving 4.6 days on hand.
Corvale General holds 157 units of the same presentation with daily use of 8.5, giving 18.4 days on hand.
The rule‑based ranking selects transferring 37 units of 1 mL/mL 250 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East as the top option.
After the transfer Corvale General would retain about two weeks of supply and Corvale East would reach approximately 9 days.
Both sites' current supply for this presentation is labeled by Bryant Ranch Prepack (NDC 72162224502).
No FDA shortage posting exists, so the buyer should execute the transfer and monitor daily use at both locations.

memory.text: Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.

Decision on cisplatin: transfer cisplatin between Corvale hospitals weekly instead of buying grey-market stock. Rationale: Grey-market offers were 6 to 10 times contract price with unverifiable pedigree (demo history). Approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD.
